1.x: Also first in Andhra: a **night school**, a **Theosophical High School**, **co-education**.
**Evils fought:** the ban on widow remarriage, child marriage, **dowry, bride-price**, caste, superstition, **nautch/Bhogam**, **official corruption**; scientific education was one of his aims.
**Methods:** journals and satire, lectures, schools, remarriages at his own cost, widow homes, prayer without idols – the **press, not direct politics**.
**Social laws:** Sati Regulation 1829 (Bentinck); Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856 (Canning); Native Marriage Act 1872; Age of Consent Act 1891 (Lansdowne).

6.x: Gurajada Appa Rao (1861-1915)

**Kanyasulkam** – social play on **bride-price** and child marriage, in spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu, **Srikakulam dialect**; written 1890, **first staged 13 Aug 1892** (Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham, Vizianagaram), **published 1897** (Vavilla), 2nd edition 1909 dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati**.
**Characters:** **Madhuravani** – reformed courtesan; **Girisham** – educated fraud; Ramappa Pantulu – hypocrite; Buchamma – widow; **Soujanya Rao** – reformer.

**Other works:** **Mutyala Saralu** (1910, new metre), **Diddubatu** (first modern Telugu short story), **Purnamma** (girl married off for money), Kanyaka; Saranga Dhara (1883) – English poem with brother Shyamala Rao.
Song **Desamunu Preminchumanna** – "Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi" (a country is its people, not its soil).
**Patron court:** **Vizianagaram** (Ananda Gajapati); title Navayuga Vaitalikudu; worked alongside **Veeresalingam** in the literary and cultural renaissance.

**Works:** **A Memorandum on Modern Telugu**, Bala Kavi Saranyam; monthly **Telugu (1919)**.
